headline: Receipt-backed task state improves agent workflow reliability in bounded tests, with matcher-dependent failures
summary: The 2026-09-22 preprint compares how an LLM agent handles assigned-work state when it is left in the transcript, displayed as a checklist, turned into per-turn directives or enforced by a gate that rejects state-violating actions. The authors report that receipt-backed directives and enforcement raise strict task-lifecycle success in controlled episodes, with gains varying by model and reasoning regime. In one tau-squared-bench airline case, enforcement raises Qwen3-235B pass at one from 0.39 to 0.54; on PM-Bench, showing the record can match or outperform gates, while matcher-based enforcement hurts a smaller model on semantic cue tasks. These are author-reported, bounded results: enforcement depends on correct compiled state and request matching, and the study does not establish general deployed-agent reliability.
